newsitem.title: USA: USDA crop report seen bearish for NYCE cotton.
newsitem.headline: USDA crop report seen bearish for NYCE cotton.

text.p: Analysts and traders said the U.S. Department of Agriculture's January cotton crop production report released Thursday morning was viewed as slightly negative and could weigh on NYCE cotton futures.

The USDA estimated U.S. 1996/97 cotton production at 18.951 480-lb bales, up one percent over the 18.738 million bales estimated in December. This would be the second largest production on record, the USDA said.
"It was mildly bearish," Prudential Securities analyst Ernest Simon said. "It was not much of a rise in production."

As expected, the Texas crop accounted for much of the rise in output. The USDA increased its forecast from a month ago by 150,000 bales to 4.35 million bales. Georgia's production was also revised upward at 2.1 million bales, a rise of 100,000 bales compared with last month's forecast.
Yield was seen at a record high 709 pounds per harvested acre, up from 704 pounds forecast last month.
But some market participants said the futures market reaction may be muted until with the USDA releases its world supply/demand forecast on Friday.
"The USDA report was negative but I do not expect much of a reaction," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "I think people will wait for the supply/demand numbers tomorrow."
Ganes expects the USDA to revise downward some of its comsumption numbers overseas, especially in China, which could also pressure the cotton futures market.
